cited_details.statement: Person search aims to retrieve instances of a queried individual from a large corpus of uncropped scene images, which is fundamental to applications in public safety, missing-person search, and forensic video analysis [https://github.com/ShuangLI59/person_search].

The shift from "match cropped boxes" to "search whole scenes" introduces substantial new difficulties, including misalignment between detection and identification objectives, occlusion, and the lack of dense identity labels in scene images [http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html].

introduced the first end-to-end deep learning framework for person search, jointly optimizing detection and re-identification within a single convolutional neural network [https://github.com/ShuangLI59/person_search, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320968559_Joint_Detection_and_Identification_Feature_Learning_for_Person_Search].

introduced the first end-to-end deep learning framework for person search, jointly optimizing detection and re-identification within a single convolutional neural network [https://github.com/ShuangLI59/person_search, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320968559_Joint_Detection_and_Identification_Feature_Learning_for_Person_Search].

To handle the fact that scene images contain many unlabeled identities, the authors proposed a *Random Sampling Softmax loss* to effectively train the model under the supervision of sparse and unbalanced labels [http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html].

Their model was trained and evaluated on the CUHK-SYSU dataset, which contains 18,184 images, 8,432 persons, and 99,809 annotated bounding boxes collected from movie scenes and street-view cameras, providing both the scale and the scene diversity that prior re-ID benchmarks lacked [http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html].

introduced a *mask-guided two-stream CNN model* that adds a segmentation branch to the detection network so that the re-identification stream receives features computed on the person mask rather than the full proposal [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

proposed a *multi-scale matching* approach that learns person representations at multiple resolutions and matches them across scales when comparing a query against a gallery [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

introduced *Relational Context-Aware Agents (RCAA)* that encode the relationships between a candidate person and its surrounding context (other people, objects, and scene elements) and use these relational cues to refine the re-identification score [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

A representative method proposes an *Asymmetric Cross-Scale Alignment* that addresses the fact that textual descriptions often refer to both global appearance and local details, while visual features must be extracted from proposals at different scales [https://cronfa.swan.ac.uk/Record/cronfa62251/Download/62251__26475__9db5b190500e40af9bfe9f45e66bbb4f.pdf].
demonstrated that sharing backbone features between the detector and the re-ID head forces the network to encode both localization and identity cues [https://github.com/ShuangLI59/person_search].

argued that a bounding box is a coarse foreground indicator and proposed to compute the re-ID feature only on a segmentation mask, eliminating background noise and aligning the re-ID input with the actual person silhouette [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

observed that identity-discriminative cues are distributed across scales—faces at high resolution, clothing at medium, gait/body shape at low—and learned a multi-scale matching scheme that aggregates evidence across resolutions [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

A complementary perspective is provided by the identity-regression literature, which notes that most existing re-ID methods are unsuitable for real-world deployment due to two specific reasons: *unscalability to large population size*, and *inadaptability over time* [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6411216/].

is the canonical metric-learning component for end-to-end person search: it compares the feature of each detected person against a lookup table of labeled identity prototypes, exploits a pool of unlabeled features to provide negative evidence, and is trained under the supervision of sparse and unbalanced labels [http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html].
The *Triplet Online Instance Matching (TOIM) loss* was proposed to address this gap by combining the advantages of OIM and the triplet loss [https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10560].

TOIM retains the OIM lookup-table machinery to handle the large and unbalanced label space typical of person search, but augments it with hard-sample mining to accelerate convergence and improve accuracy [https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10560].

Importantly, TOIM is designed to be trained online alongside the joint detection-and-identification pipeline, making it suitable for end-to-end person search; the authors also introduce the UESTC-PR benchmark to evaluate the loss in surveillance-scale settings [https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10560].

The identity-regression formulation of re-ID attacks the same challenge from a different angle: instead of treating each gallery identity as a discrete class, it maps features into a continuous identity space in which distance has a direct semantic interpretation, and is explicitly motivated by the *unscalability* of classification-based losses to large populations and their *inadaptability* over time [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6411216/].

Xiao et al.'s end-to-end CNN is the canonical example: detection and re-identification share the same backbone and ROI features, so gradients from the identification loss flow back into the detector and shape its representations toward identity-preserving crops [https://github.com/ShuangLI59/person_search].
TOIM extends this idea by providing a richer, hard-sample-aware identification signal during joint training, leading to more identity-discriminative proposals [https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10560].

takes a different route, using a separate segmentation branch to define a person mask that overrides the box boundary and forces the re-ID stream to attend to the actual person silhouette rather than the box [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

Relational context-aware methods such as RCAA further mitigate the inconsistency by scoring a candidate not only on its own appearance but also on its relationship to surrounding people and scene elements, which provides a useful fallback when the candidate box itself is imperfect [https://github.com/wangxiao5791509/Person-Search-Paper-List].

It contains 18,184 images, 8,432 identities, and 99,809 annotated pedestrian bounding boxes, collected from a wide range of movie scenes and street-view cameras, with substantial variation in pose, illumination, occlusion, and background [http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html].

Beyond CUHK-SYSU, the field has produced additional benchmarks and methods targeting scalability and adaptability over time, motivated by the need to deploy re-ID systems in evolving real-world populations [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6411216/].
